title: TrainSDC: Characterizing and Mitigating Silent Data Corruption in Large Language Model Training
abstract: arXiv:2608.30769v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM training is increasingly vulnerable to silent data corruption (SDC), yet existing protection methods largely treat Transformer computations uniformly because their vulnerability remains poorly understood. We present the first systematic characterization of SDC vulnerability across major computation interfaces in both the forward and backward passes of Transformer training. Our analysis reveals two distinct error propagation mechanisms: forward-pass vulnerability is highly location dependent, with faults on the Q/K path producing persistent training deviations, whereas backward-pass vulnerability is largely governed by gradient exponent distributions rather than computation locations. Motivated by these observations, we propose TrainSDC, a characterization-guided protection framework consisting of Q/K-path recomputation, residual-gain monitoring, and exponent-aware gradient scaling. tldr: 该论文首次系统表征了大语言模型训练中静默数据损坏的脆弱性，发现前向传播的脆弱性高度依赖计算位置而反向传播主要由梯度指数分布决定，并据此提出了包含Q/K路径重计算、残差增益监测和指数感知梯度缩放的保护框架TrainSDC。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic characterization of SDC vulnerability in LLM training, revealing that forward-pass vulnerability is location-dependent while backward-pass vulnerability is governed by gradient exponent distributions, and proposes TrainSDC, a protection framework combining Q/K-path recomputation, residual-gain monitoring, and exponent-aware gradient scaling.
